I’ve always been fascinated by why some people and teams seem to move forward with ease while others, despite all the effort, stay stuck.
 
Long before I became a coach, I spent over 20 years producing advertising campaigns. My job wasn’t just to make great films. It was to spot what wasn’t working, bring the right people together and find better ways to make things happen. I still do exactly that today.
 
Over the past decade I’ve worked with executives and leadership teams across the Middle East, and one thing has become very clear. People don’t change because someone gives them better advice. They change when they experience something that gives them their own proof.
 
That’s why I created the EXP Method™.  EXP is an evidence-based coaching approach built around carefully designed experiences that help people uncover blind spots, challenge old assumptions and create their own evidence for change.

Sometimes that’s helping a leadership team discover the pattern that’s been slowing decisions for years.
 
Sometimes it’s a simple exercise that makes someone realise they’re capable of far more than they believed just a few minutes earlier.
 
Those moments matter because once people prove something to themselves, they rarely go back to thinking the same way.  If that resonates with you, let’s connect. 

Founder, EXP Method™

One of the things I work on is something I call ‘Leadership Architecture’. It’s not unusual for entrepreneurs to build business – clever, smart businesses – with their genius. They carve out niches in their industry, build reputation which becomes their natural sales generation.

But it doesn’t always stay that way. Very often, their myopic view of the world is such that they think ‘their way is the way’. They embrace technology and AI in a way they know and understand, they stay with their loyal team who scramble and often get left behind. Many make decisions to protect their own roles, some are simply in the wrong role causing harm to the business. I see terrible uses of technology and AI which very often makes for a shorter meeting and a cull of that supplier.

Sometimes they call someone like me to help them see the wider picture. That's Leadership Architecture. That some of their leaders need to be deployed in other roles or elsewhere, that new talent needs to be brought in (or developed) to help their business grow in ways they never thought possible, to evolve, embrace new pillars within their sector to protect the next generation of their business. To survive. In a market like the UAE right now, that’s not a nice to have.

I help leaders make the really tough calls, have the really tough conversations, and ask the tough questions. They’re tough because really you know the answers and the output from them which is often uncomfortable. I don’t need to be an expert in what you do, that’s you. I’ll guide you to making the right decisions to building a high performance business, beyond what you thought possible.

If you’ve got this far, it might mean that this resonates, we’re here to guide you, and have the transformational conversations.

🌊 Botswana is home to the Okavango Delta, the world’s largest inland delta. We loved seeing it from above during a scenic flight.

🦁 Around 40% of the country is protected through national parks and wildlife reserves.

👥 With just over 2.5 million people living in a country the size of France, Botswana is one of the most sparsely populated countries in the world.

💎 It is one of the world’s biggest diamond producers - diamonds account for around 80% of Botswana’s export earnings and have played a major role in transforming the country’s economy since independence.

🦓 The Makgadikgadi salt pans in Botswana are among the largest salt flats on Earth, remnants of an ancient lake.

❤️ “Botho” is a core national value, meaning humanity, kindness, and respect for others.

shortlist.author: self
shortlist.quote:
WD PERSPECTIVE

Growth isn’t built on always getting it right.
It’s built on trying again.

Our brains are wired to prioritise safety. When we’re faced with uncertainty, they naturally encourage us towards what’s familiar and predictable.

That instinct has helped us survive. But in modern life, uncertainty is often where growth begins.

Whether you’re launching a business, introducing a new service, investing in equipment, hiring your first employee, returning from injury, preparing for competition, or learning a new skill - uncertainty is very much part of the process.

Confidence rarely comes first. It develops through experience.

Each time we step into uncertainty and discover we’re capable of navigating it, our brains begin to update their expectations. Over time, what once felt unfamiliar becomes more familiar, and what once felt risky feels increasingly manageable.

The same principle applies to business.

Growth often means making decisions without complete certainty. Testing new ideas. Refining systems. Investing in people. Adapting to change.

Strategy doesn’t eliminate uncertainty. It helps us navigate it with greater clarity, confidence and purpose.

At Wellness Division we work alongside wellness businesses as they make those decisions - helping them build the strategy, systems and confidence to keep moving forwards.

Because growth isn’t about waiting until you’re certain. It’s about knowing how to take the next step.

shortlist.author: self
shortlist.quote:
She did not build her signature brand at 22.
She built it at 40.

Before everybody knew Vera Wang’s name, she had already built multiple identities.

First, she was a competitive figure skater.

Then she worked for Vogue and Ralph Lauren.

After all of these experiences, she launched the business that made her iconic.

Now we are coming to the part that every corporate professional needs to hear.

Because so many people panic when their first path does not become their final path.

I have coached hundreds of experienced professionals through career reinvention.

Many of them were thinking at the beginning:
“I’m behind.”
“If I change direction now, I’m starting from zero.

When you look at Vera Wang’s story, it will tell you the opposite.

A career with twists and turns does not mean you are lost.

Career paths are not linear.
There is no such thing.

At each point, you have built something: better taste, judgment, and the experience your next chapter will be built on.

Many mid-senior professionals in transition see their past experience as random.
But this is not true.

The years in the wrong room, the years in the good-but-not-quite-right role, the years when you were learning without fully arriving…

Those years often become the foundation of your most aligned work.

Vera Wang did not “start late.”

She started when her experience, identity, and perspective were finally strong enough to create something unique.

Career reinvention is all about bringing the pieces of your past together and making a new puzzle.

Connecting the dots in a magical way.

Understanding how to use your past for your future.

This is your reminder when your career path has been non-linear:
Your first careers are not the destination.
They have been preparing you for what comes next.

Have you seen someone build their next career chapter with courage?

shortlist.author: self
shortlist.quote:
Every small business knows this scenario: a customer messages at 11pm, no one replies, and the sale goes to a competitor.
That question is exactly what led me to build WaaAgent.
It's not just another chatbot it's an agent that holds full context about a business (products, images, pricing), takes on a fully customizable persona, and responds in a natural, human like way like a real employee who knows every detail of the business.
Built with Node.js + whatsapp-web.js, plus:
→ Multi-provider AI failover so the work never stops
→ Full dashboard to manage contacts and campaigns
→ Smart proactive follow-up for contacts who went quiet
→ Human-like interaction with typing delays and conversational memory
I decided to open-source the idea and the code — not to sell it, but because I want to see where the tech community takes it.
Next on the roadmap:
→ Voice message understanding and transcription
→ AI-generated voice replies sent directly through WhatsApp
→ Richer multimodal interactions beyond text
GitHub: https://lnkd.in/egAKGiWa
#AI #WhatsApp #OpenSource #BuildInPublic #NodeJS

shortlist.author: self
shortlist.quote:
What do you measure in your business?

If you don’t measure the critical elements of your business, you have no way of knowing where you are or where you're headed. Too much data can be just as bad as too little. It's not what you measure that's important but the meaning you give each measurement. 

My Top Tips  on what and how to measure:- 
🌟 Focus on activity. It's easy to fixate on results but it's activity that leads to success. 
🌟 People. Without a team it's impossible to scale a business. How are you leveraging your people? 
🌟 Customer satisfaction. What's happening internally can never be more important than what your market is telling you. 
🌟 Productivity. How can you make your processes smoother, more consistent, less costly? 
🌟 Retention. Don't put all your focus on new clients. Look at retention metrics, cost of acquisition and client lifetime spend. 
🌟 Profit over revenue. The revenue number is the one everyone talks about but it's profit that'll keep you in business. 
🌟 Your expectations. What do you want from your business and how do you define success? 

Hope you have a productive day!
